post.description:
Accept a delivery once PayPal confirms its signature; a repeat delivery is a no-op.

The event is stored and its processing queued in one transaction before the 2xx that stops
PayPal's retries. A 400 answers headers or a body that cannot be PayPal's, checked first so
they cost no PayPal call, or a signature PayPal rejects; an error reaching PayPal or the
database surfaces as a 500 so PayPal delivers the event again later.
Queue a stored event for processing again, as if it had just arrived.
An empty cart that the given wallet will pay for.

put.description: Set how many of a product in a size the cart holds; 0 removes the line.

post.description:
Pay for the cart from its wallet; calling again returns the order already placed.

A request signed by a registered agent places an agent order under the buyer's mandate and
the merchant's policy; a 403 names what refused it. An unsigned request is the buyer's own.
Begin saving the buyer's PayPal wallet; send the buyer to the approve URL.

Finish saving the wallet once the buyer has returned from PayPal.

A 422 means PayPal refused the setup token (unknown, unapproved, or already used); a 502
means PayPal failed to answer.

Mark a paid order shipped: its tracking goes onto the PayPal capture.

A 409 means the order is not captured or already shipped; a 422 means PayPal refused the
tracking; a 502 means PayPal failed to answer.

get.description: The disputes PayPal opened on the store's payments, newest first.

post.description:
Read the dispute from PayPal now, as a webhook would.

A 404 means the dispute names a payment that is none of the shop's orders; a 422 names
what PayPal refused.

get.description: Palisade's answer to the dispute as it stands: what it can do next, and the evidence so far.

post.description:
Write the notes and the record now, as the job would on PayPal's cue.

A 502 means Claude did not deliver the notes.

Approve the prepared evidence and send what PayPal takes now.

An inquiry that must become a claim is escalated, and the evidence follows once the claim
takes it. A 409 means the evidence was filed or refused already; a 422 names what PayPal
refused.

200.description: The record PDF Palisade attached to the evidence.

get.description: The merchant's policy in force: the rules agents are checked against, and the filing mode.

put.description: Choose whether Palisade waits for the merchant before filing evidence, or files on its own.

post.description:
Sandbox simulator: file a dispute on a paid demo-buyer order as the demo buyer.

A 409 means the order cannot be disputed this way, or PayPal's search does not list the
payment yet; a 422 means PayPal refused the dispute.

Sandbox simulator: have PayPal decide the dispute for the seller or the buyer.

A 409 means PayPal does not offer a decision yet.

An agent asks the buyer for a mandate; the answer holds the key and the consent link.

Only a signed agent request may ask. A 404 names a wallet or cart that cannot be used; a 422
a request that does not fit its kind, such as a cart mandate whose cap is not the cart total.

A challenge and the options for a new passkey that signs for this mandate's wallet.

The options are for `navigator.credentials.create()`. A 403 means the mandate key is
missing or wrong.

get.description:
The browser options that make the given passkey sign this mandate.

A 404 names a passkey that does not sign for this mandate's wallet; register a new one.

post.description:
The buyer signs the mandate with a passkey, or the demo signer (simulated) for the demo buyer.

A 409 means it is answered already or its cart changed since the request.
Keep the passkey the browser created; its id signs that wallet's mandates from now on.

get.description: The agent-side events the store recorded, newest first; `kind` narrows them to one kind.
The agent-side events behind one order, oldest first, from the shopper's request on.
What was recorded about one dispute, oldest first; empty for a dispute never stored.
Answers 204 when the access code is right; the chat panel's code screen checks it here.

post.description:
Start a conversation paid from the wallet; a 404 names a wallet or cart that cannot be used.

The answer carries the conversation's key, handed out this once; reading or continuing the
conversation needs it.

get.description:
The conversation, for the holder of its key.

A 401 means the chat access code is wrong; a 403 means the conversation key is.

post.description:
Send the shopper's message and stream the agent's turn.

An answer on the consent page needs no message: the API carries the conversation on by
itself, and the conversation shows that turn as it runs. A 401 means the chat access code
is wrong; a 403 means the conversation's key is missing or wrong. A 404 names a
conversation or cart that cannot be used. A 409 means the agent is still answering.

200.description: The agent's turn as server-sent events, ending with `done` or `error`.

get.description:
What every platform probe calls: the process answers.

It reads nothing, so a database outage neither restarts the replica nor takes it out of rotation.
Whether this replica reaches its database; the release workflow checks it after a deploy.

503.description: The database did not answer in time.

Activity.title: Activity
Activity.description:
An activity row as the console reads it.

The conversation it belongs to stays server-side: a conversation id plus the shared chat
code would open another shopper's chat. Mandate and order ids are safe to show, because
neither can be acted on without the mandate's key or a signed mandate.

Cart.title: Cart
Cart.description:
A cart as the shop reads it.

The wallet it pays with stays server-side: a cart id reached through an order's page must
not hand out a wallet that another cart could charge.

CheckoutRequest.title: CheckoutRequest
CheckoutRequest.description:
What an agent sends with a checkout: the buyer-signed mandate that covers it.

The key is the one the agent got when it asked for the mandate.

CreatedConversation.title: CreatedConversation
CreatedConversation.description: A new conversation with the key that opens it; the key is handed out this once.

Dispute.title: Dispute
Dispute.description:
A dispute as its console page shows it.

The buyer's name, email, and PayPal account stay server-side; the order already names its
wallet.

DisputeEvidence.title: DisputeEvidence
DisputeEvidence.description: One item on PayPal's evidence list: a party's filing, or what PayPal asks a party for.

DisputeSummary.title: DisputeSummary
DisputeSummary.description: A dispute as the console's list shows it.

DoneEvent.title: DoneEvent
DoneEvent.description: The turn as stored, the cart the agent is filling, and the mandate it now waits on.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: One answer Palisade prepared, as the console shows it; the PDF comes from its own route.

IssuedMandate.title: IssuedMandate
IssuedMandate.description:
A new mandate as its requesting agent gets it: the one time its key is handed out.

`consent_path` carries the key after `#`, so browsers send it to no server and no Referer.

LineChange.title: LineChange
LineChange.description: A product in a size and the quantity wanted; 0 removes the line.

LinkStart.title: LinkStart
LinkStart.description: Where to send the buyer to approve the link, and the token to confirm with afterwards.

LiveTurn.title: LiveTurn
LiveTurn.description: The turn still running, as far as it got: saved at each tool call, so any reader sees it.

Mandate.title: Mandate
Mandate.description:
A mandate as the consent page and the agent read it; anyone holding its id may read it.

The cart it covers stays server-side, as on orders: an open cart's id is all it takes to
change it or check it out, and a mandate id is public on the activity feed. Answering or
spending the mandate takes the key only its requesting agent got.

MandateRequest.title: MandateRequest
MandateRequest.description: What an agent asks the buyer to allow.

MandateSummary.title: MandateSummary
MandateSummary.description: The mandate as an order carries it, decoded for the console.

Money.title: Money
Money.description: An amount in PayPal's shape, so an order line can carry it unchanged.

Order.title: Order
Order.description:
An order as its public page shows it.

The cart it came from stays server-side: a declined order reopens its cart, and an open
cart's id is all it takes to fill it and pay from its wallet.

paypal_event.title: Paypal Event
paypal_event.description: The PayPal event a webhook row records; None on a checkout or repair row.

OrderSummary.title: OrderSummary
OrderSummary.description: An order as the console's list shows it, without its lines, events, and PayPal calls.

PhotoCredit.title: PhotoCredit
PhotoCredit.description: Who took the product photo and where it lives on Unsplash.

RegistrationStart.title: RegistrationStart
RegistrationStart.description: What the browser's `navigator.credentials.create()` needs, and the challenge to return.

MandateKey.description: The key the requesting agent got with the mandate, in its consent link after `#key=`.
MandateKey.name: X-Mandate-Key

ChatKey.description: The access code the chat panel asks for, sent with every chat request.
ChatKey.name: X-Chat-Key

ConversationKey.description: The key a conversation was created with, sent when reading or continuing it.
ConversationKey.name: X-Conversation-Key
